name: Dieu De Pagoda
kicker: National pagoda on the Gia Hoi river
summary: Cross to the gate of Diệu Đế on the Hộ Thành river, at 100B Bạch Đằng in Phú Cát, near Gia Hội bridge. The city page dates the work to the third month of Thiệu Trị 4, 1844, on the future king’s garden. It is one of three Nguyễn national pagodas still in Hue. The fee and the hours are check on arrival.
getThere: 100B Bạch Đằng, near Gia Hội bridge. Minutes are check on arrival.
heroCaption: The gate of Dieu De from the river

notice.title: No published fee, and no published hour
notice.body: The city page gives the address and the 1844 date. It does not give a ticket or a closing time. Confirm the gate when you arrive.

body: The city page places Diệu Đế on the Hộ Thành river, which Hue also calls the Gia Hội or Đông Ba river, at 100B Bạch Đằng, phường Phú Cát, near Gia Hội bridge. It is one of three Nguyễn national pagodas still standing in Hue.

The same page says the pagoda was built up in the third month of Thiệu Trị 4, 1844, on the garden of Phúc Quốc Công, later Emperor Thiệu Trị. An English page on the same site mixes in an 1807 date and a 5,000 square metre platform. Those lines disagree with the Vietnamese city page. This guide follows the 1844 account.
The fee and the hours are check on arrival. The walk from the south bank, across toward Gia Hội bridge, has no published minute count.

gettingThere: From the south bank, cross toward Gia Hội bridge and 100B Bạch Đằng, Phú Cát. The minutes are check on arrival.

legs.heading: From the south bank
legs.body: Toward Gia Hội bridge and Bạch Đằng. No published minute count. Check on arrival.

closed: No closing day is published. Confirm on arrival.
admissionNote: Check on arrival. No fee is printed on the city page.
